name: exp3-iter0-critique
description: Exp3 iter-0 critique of heading_direction_range_extrapolation — data layout and 8 raw-slice stats submitted
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp3 iter 0 (2026-10-31): the data has 6750 rows and 218 sets, mostly scattered 4-example sets. Each trial_index has 15 rows (about 15 people × 450 trials), and there is no participant_id. Observed patterns: the yes rate falls from 0.51 to 0.35 over the session; 70,10,88,40 gets only 0.13 yes despite being all even; final-digit rules with one exception get 0.89 yes; shown examples get 0.90 yes.
I submitted 8 stats: early-minus-late drift, near first vs near last example, 3-of-4 last-digit match, wide-span interior, single-example distance gradient, far extrapolation from 2-example sets, same-parity match, and target-is-example. description: Exp3 iter-1 critique of heading_extrapolation_weber_width — 8 new raw-slice stats (reversal, doubling, AP lattice, decade boundary, etc.); iter-0 got 0/8

  type: project
---

- digit reversal (obs 0.46)
- double/half of an example (0.49)
- AP lattice on-minus-off (+0.10)

- decade boundary in near extrapolation (+0.07)

metadata:
  type: project
---
Iter-1 critique (2026-10-31) found 0/8 significant; the nearest misses were double/half yes (obs above null, z=1.86) and per-set yes-rate SD (obs below null, z=-1.83).

---
name: exp3-iter3-position-decaying-evidence
description: Exp3 iter-3 cand_0 — example evidence scaled exp(rho*(k-1)) has rho≈+0.015 (null); with an equal range prior it ties the incumbent at MAP; exact sparse (set, coverage-pattern, width) class tabulation gives 14 ms/grad
metadata:
  type: project
---
Exp3 iter 3, candidate_0 (2026-10-31), exploratory order slot. Submitted `position_decaying_example_evidence`: each example's log-evidence is scaled by exp(rho*(k-1)) (total not conserved), the range prior is equal (no Weber, heading or upward terms), sampling is with replacement, plus digit sums and a lapse.
- MAP on the incumbent base (exact grid): rho=0 gives -3189.44, free rho gives -3188.65 (rho +0.02). Weber+heading+upward together are worth only about 1 nat.
- The submitted model's MAP is -3190.47 against the incumbent's -3190.30, with 3 fewer parameters. Its pool RMSE is at least 0.0059 vs the incumbent, heading_weber, digit_sum_open_ended and example_blind_lapse. The smoke fit gave -3192.4.
- So rho does not capture the prefix-extension critique: the decay comes out null.
Speed trick: under an equal range prior, an interval's evidence depends only on its (contiguous sorted-example coverage pattern, width). Flatten the nonzero (set, pattern, width) classes (~67k) and the (cell, class) entries (~268k) and use inc_subtensor segment sums. That is 14 ms/grad, exact; the dense 100x100 grid took 310 ms.
PITFALL: compile_fn on raw module-level tensors draws the RVs at random; use model.replace_rvs_by_values first.
See [[exp3-iter3-critique]], [[number-game-ceiling]].

# name: prefix_extension_yes_change
# description: For 4-example sets whose first three examples are also shown as a 3-example set, yes rate on the 4-example set minus the 3-example set over the same non-example targets; observed above null means adding a fourth example narrows generalization less (or broadens it more) than the model predicts.
def test_statistic(df):
    x = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")
    t = df["target"].astype(int)
    r = df["rating"].astype(float)
    n = x.notna().sum(axis=1)
    mn = x.min(axis=1)
    mx = x.max(axis=1)
    isin = x.eq(t, axis=0).any(axis=1)
    nd = x.sub(t, axis=0).abs().min(axis=1)
    s = df["number_set"].astype(str)
    pre = s.where(n == 4).str.rsplit(",", n=1).str[0]
    k = pd.DataFrame({"s": s, "t": t, "r": r, "n": n, "pre": pre, "isin": isin})
    k = k[~k["isin"]]
    three = k[k["n"] == 3].groupby(["s", "t"])["r"].mean().rename("r3").reset_index().rename(columns={"s": "pre"})
    four = k[k["n"] == 4].groupby(["pre", "t"])["r"].mean().rename("r4").reset_index()
    m = four.merge(three, on=["pre", "t"])
    v = (m["r4"] - m["r3"]).mean() if len(m) else 0.0
    return float(0.0 if (v is None or not np.isfinite(v)) else v)

g=d.groupby('number_set').agg(nt=('target','nunique'),n=('rating','size'),y=('rating','mean'))

sets=d.number_set.unique()
S={x:frozenset(map(int,x.split(','))) for x in sets}
c=0
for a in sets:
  for b in sets:
    if S[b]<S[a] and len(S[b])==1:
      ta=set(d[d.number_set==a].target); tb=set(d[d.number_set==b].target)
      c+=len((ta&tb)-S[a])
print('1ex-subset common targets',c)
"

content.text:
I wrote the 8 test statistics to `experiment3/model_loop/iter_4/critique/test_stats/`. Each one ran on the observed data, returned a finite number, and took about 0.02 s, with no import lines. I didn't run the posterior-predictive check; the pipeline does that.

Last round, one statistic out of 8 was significant: adding a fourth example widened generalization more than the model expected (p = 0.014). The new incumbent's fitted decay rate came out at about zero, so it probably doesn't fix that. It also drops the earlier Weber, heading and upward range terms. So this round re-tests that finding and checks whether dropping those terms left gaps.

| Statistic | Observed | What a discrepancy would mean |
|---|---|---|
| `rule_violating_interior_yes` | 0.114 (385 rows) | Below the model's prediction: when the examples share a final digit or a multiple, people reject in-span targets that break it more firmly than the model's ranges allow. |
| `rule_matching_target_yes` | 0.96 (125 rows) | Above the model's prediction: people accept targets with the shared final digit more fully than the model does. |
| `single_example_above_minus_below` | −0.106 | Tests up/down asymmetry around a single example, which the equal-range prior treats as symmetric. Observed above the model means more upward extension than predicted. |
| `near_extrapolation_large_minus_small_edge` | +0.145 | Above the model's prediction: people generalize further around large numbers (the dropped Weber effect). |
| `fourth_example_prefix_broadening` | 0.287 | Last round's significant statistic, re-tested unchanged against the new model. It rests almost entirely on 31,3,1 → 31,3,1,15. |
| `two_example_interior_wide_minus_narrow_gap` | −0.183 | Compares how often people say yes between two examples when the gap is wide (≥40) versus narrow (≤20). |
| `interior_yes_4ex_minus_2ex_matched_span` | −0.065 | Above the model's prediction: extra examples tighten in-span answers less than predicted (the decay mechanism). |
| `single_example_multiple_target_yes` | +0.367 | Above the model's prediction: people generalize to multiples of a lone example more than the rule prior predicts. |

The fourth-example statistic is the same as last round's under a new name. It's in again because nothing in the new model should fix that miss. The single-example multiples slice is the thinnest (65 and 85 rows). I saved a note on this round to the agent memory.
